```sql
SELECT c.id,
       c.email,
       c.company,
       c.country_code,
       sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
       count(*)           AS order_count,
       CASE WHEN bool_or(o.created_at IS NULL) THEN NULL
            ELSE max(o.created_at)
       END                AS last_order_at
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
   AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
 GROUP BY c.id, c.email, c.company, c.country_code
HAVING (CASE WHEN bool_or(o.created_at IS NULL) THEN NULL
             ELSE max(o.created_at)
        END) >= %(from)s
   AND (CASE WHEN bool_or(o.created_at IS NULL) THEN NULL
             ELSE max(o.created_at)
        END) <  %(to)s
 ORDER BY revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De originele query materialiseerde en aggregeerde de orders van alle tenants, en scande die twee keer (totalen en DISTINCT ON met sortering). Nu wordt eerst op de klanten van de tenant gefilterd en gebeurt alles in één join en aggregatie. De CASE rond `max(created_at)` bewaart het gedrag van `DISTINCT ON … created_at DESC`, waarbij een NULL bovenaan komt, ook als `created_at` nullable zou zijn.
